ai.description: This slender snake reaches 2 meters. It is bright green with distinctive black edges on its dorsal scales. A dark stripe runs behind each eye, and the tail is notably long and thin.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Ptyas nigromarginata* is the distinct black edging on its scales, which creates a noticeable "netted" or reticulated pattern.
ai.habitat: The Green Rat Snake inhabits moist, subtropical broadleaf forests and temperate mountainous regions of the Himalayas, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Green Rat Snake is primarily diurnal and arboreal, often hunting for lizards and small birds among the branches of Himalayan forests.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ptyas nigromarginata* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–12 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the spring and summer months in its Indian range.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ptyas nigromarginata* occurs in the Eastern Himalayas, ranging from Nepal through Northeast India (e.g., Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh) at elevations of 500–2,000 meters.
